title: named control keys reach the pty raw
asserts: a `key` frame resolves NAMES to bytes in the core and writes them to the pty without bracketed paste, which is what makes them keystrokes rather than text: a Backspace erases the character before it and an Enter submits the line, so the title the stand-in then sets is proof both bytes were read by the line discipline and neither was pasted. An unknown name is refused with an `error` and writes NOTHING - the failure the frame exists to prevent is the word "Escape" landing in an agent's prompt box - and a key is never worth reviving a dead session for.

steps.note: no trailing newline, and one character too many
a sequenced key acks like a sequenced input
the X is gone and the line ran, so 0x7f was ERASE and 0x0d was a carriage return - not the words Backspace and Enter typed into the line
one bad name in a batch, which refuses the whole batch
unlike an `input`, which revives a dead session to deliver a message: there is no prompt in a fresh process for a keystroke to answer
